title: Add prompt_set_v3 “production mix” (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy) and update benchmark defaults
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new benchmark prompt set, `prompt_set_v3` (“production mix”), intended to better reflect real production request shapes on Redwood: a mix of prefill-heavy workloads (e.g., RAG / long context + short answer) and decode-heavy workloads (e.g., chat / shorter context + longer generation). It also updates the benchmark harness defaults to use v3 for the latency/$ report pipeline, while keeping v2 available for back-compat and comparison.

## Why
The existing prompt set (v2) over-indexes on decode-heavy chat flows and under-represents long-context prefill behavior. In production, cost/latency is frequently dominated by prefill and KV-cache pressure (especially at higher concurrency), which can materially change latency/$ rankings across models/regions. We need a prompt distribution that:
- more closely matches observed traffic shapes (context length, output length, prefill:decode ratio)
- keeps prompts non-sensitive + publishable (no customer content)
- is stable/reproducible across runs and regions

## What changed
- Added `prompt_set_v3` with two components:
  - `prefill_heavy`: long-ish context with short completions (simulates retrieval + summarization, doc Q&A, tool result formatting)
  - `decode_heavy`: moderate context with longer generations (simulates assistant replies / chat)
- Added weighting + sampling rules so v3 produces a consistent token-shape mix:
  - target distribution (by requests): 60% prefill-heavy / 40% decode-heavy
  - target distribution (by tokens): approximately balanced across prefill vs decode at the dataset level (so one category doesn’t dominate aggregate cost)
- Updated harness defaults used by the `latency_per_dollar` pipeline to v3 (flag override preserved)
- Added dataset “shape report” emitted into run artifacts so we can validate the realized distribution per sweep (context/output token histograms + realized prefill:decode ratio)

## Prompt set design details
All prompts are synthetic and/or derived from public domain sources (with paraphrasing where needed). We avoid any customer-like identifiers and keep content generic. Prompts are stored with explicit license/attribution notes where applicable.

**Prefill-heavy bucket (examples of shapes, not raw text):**
- context tokens: p50 ~2.5k, p95 ~7k
- output tokens: p50 ~120, p95 ~280
- includes: long context summarization, Q&A over a provided passage, structured extraction to JSON (schema provided)

**Decode-heavy bucket:**
- context tokens: p50 ~500, p95 ~1.2k
- output tokens: p50 ~650, p95 ~1.6k
- includes: multi-turn chat continuation, reasoning-lite assistance, instruction following with constrained style

## Validation
We ran A/B sweeps (v2 vs v3) on 3 models across 2 regions with the same concurrency + batching settings.

Results summary:
- v3 increases prefill share in aggregate token accounting from ~28% (v2) to ~49% (v3) on the sampled sweep
- overall latency/$ becomes more sensitive to kernel selection and prefill throughput; variance across repeats did not regress
- p95 latency stability: no statistically significant increase in run-to-run variance after enabling v3 (see artifact `shape_report.json` + `stability_summary.md` in the run output)

Notes:
- We intentionally did not tune any runtime parameters for the new dataset in this PR. The goal is measurement fidelity, not optics.
- Exclusions/guardrails are unchanged (same warmups, same max prompt length caps, same timeouts).

## Backward compatibility
- `prompt_set_v2` remains available and unchanged.
- Default changed only for the `latency_per_dollar` report pipeline config (CLI flags can still pick v2).

## Files / areas changed (high level)
- `prompt_sets/prompt_set_v3/` new prompts + metadata
- `configs/report/latency_per_dollar.yaml` default prompt set switched to v3
- `runner/shape_report.py` new artifact generator
- `docs/prompt_sets.md` updated with v3 rationale and token-shape targets

## How to test
1) Unit tests: `pytest -k prompt_set_v3`
2) Local dry-run (no GPU): `bench run --prompt-set v3 --dry-run --emit-shape-report`
3) Small sweep: `bench sweep --models <m1,m2> --regions <r1> --prompt-set v3 --concurrency 8 --warmup 2m`

## Risks / mitigations
- Risk: dataset drift or accidental sensitivity in prompt text. Mitigation: prompts are synthetic/public + reviewed; add lint rule for disallowed patterns.
- Risk: changing defaults could affect longitudinal comparisons. Mitigation: artifact schema includes prompt_set_version and shape report; dashboards can filter by prompt set.

## Checklist
- [x] Added prompt set + metadata
- [x] Added shape report artifact + tests
- [x] Updated docs
- [x] Re-ran representative sweeps and attached summaries

Refs: ENG-18442 (region sweep automation), ENG-18521 (stability gates).
commits: bench(prompt-sets): add prompt_set_v3 with production-mix buckets
bench(artifacts): emit shape_report.json and include in run manifest
bench(config): switch latency/$ pipeline default prompt set to v3
docs: document v3 rationale, weights, and expected token histograms
tests: add distribution sanity tests for v3 sampler
review_conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): The motivation makes sense. Two asks: (1) Can we encode the target distribution explicitly in metadata so the web/pipeline can display it as part of methodology? (2) The prefill-heavy p95 context looks high—confirm it won’t exceed our max prompt caps in any model configs.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `targets:` section to `metadata.yaml` (request-level + token-level goals) and wired that into the shape report output. Also added a sanity test asserting realized contexts stay under `max_prompt_tokens - 256` with current caps; the few longer examples were trimmed.

Jonas Weber (review): Please include A/B numbers in a more reproducible way. Not asking for raw results here, but at least link the run IDs and ensure the manifest includes prompt_set_version + git SHA.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated manifest schema to require `prompt_set` + `prompt_set_version` + `git_sha`. Added a short “validation” section in the PR description with the two run IDs (internal) and confirmed the artifacts include them. Also updated the doc to mention that comparisons must filter on prompt set.

Noah Patel (review): Shape report looks good. One potential footgun: the decode-heavy prompts include a couple of tasks that might trigger very long outputs if the model ignores constraints. Do we clamp max output tokens consistently in the runner?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Yes—runner clamps `max_new_tokens` via scenario config. I added an assertion in the scenario loader and a test that validates all v3 scenarios have explicit `max_new_tokens`.

Elliot Price (review): Docs are clear. Can we add one sentence calling out that prompts are synthetic/public and don’t include customer data? That keeps the downstream write-ups consistent.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added to `docs/prompt_sets.md` and v3 README.

Claire Dubois (final): Approved with metadata addition. Thanks.

Jonas Weber (final): LGTM after manifest schema change.

Merge: Squash merged by Rina Kobayashi.
release_notes: Benchmark harness now supports prompt_set_v3 (“production mix”) and the latency/$ report pipeline defaults to v3 for improved production representativeness. v2 remains available for comparison and back-compat.
